properties.headline: Severe Thunderstorm Warning issued October 14 at 2:02PM CDT until October 14 at 2:45PM CDT by NWS Lubbock TX
properties.description:
At 201 PM CDT, a severe thunderstorm was located 11 miles east of
Guthrie, moving northeast at 15 mph.

HAZARD...70 mph wind gusts and half dollar size hail.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Hail damage to vehicles is expected. Expect considerable
tree damage. Wind damage is also likely to mobile homes,
roofs, and outbuildings.

This severe thunderstorm will remain over mainly rural areas of
northeastern King County.
properties.instruction:
For your protection move to an interior room on the lowest floor of a
building.

Torrential rainfall is occurring with this storm, and may lead to
flash flooding. Do not drive your vehicle through flooded roadways.

properties.headline: Flood Watch issued October 14 at 1:47PM CDT until October 16 at 7:00AM CDT by NWS Austin/San Antonio TX
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is possible.

* WHERE...Val Verde County.

* WHEN...From Thursday afternoon through Friday morning.

* IMPACTS...There is a potential for life threatening flooding
somewhere in the watch area. Excessive runoff may result in
flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying and
flood-prone locations. Creeks and streams may rise out of their
banks.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Between 1 to 3 inches of rainfall, with isolated amounts of 6
inches possible.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
You should monitor later forecasts and be alert for possible Flood
Warnings. Those living in areas prone to flooding should be prepared
to take action should flooding develop.

properties.description:
* WHAT...Flash flooding caused by excessive rainfall is possible.

* WHERE...A portion of west central Texas, including the following
counties, Callahan, Coke, Coleman, Concho, Crockett, Fisher,
Haskell, Irion, Jones, Nolan, Runnels, Schleicher, Shackelford,
Sterling, Sutton, Taylor, Throckmorton and Tom Green.

crossings may be flooded.

- There is an increased danger to lives and property due to flash
flooding. Flash flooding is likely and considerable flash

highly efficient rain showers and thunderstorms to the area,
increasing flood potential Thursday afternoon into Friday
morning.

should Flash Flood Warnings be issued.

properties.headline: Special Marine Warning issued October 14 at 2:41PM EDT until October 14 at 3:15PM EDT by NWS Miami FL
properties.description:
SMWMFL

The National Weather Service in Miami has issued a

* Special Marine Warning for...
Waters from Deerfield Beach to Ocean Reef FL from 20 to 60 NM
excluding the territorial waters of Bahamas...

* Until 315 PM EDT.

* At 240 PM EDT, severe thunderstorms capable of producing
waterspouts were located along a line extending from 38 nm east of
Sunny Isles to 38 nm east of Triumph Reef to 43 nm east of Pacific
Reef, moving west at 10 knots.

HAZARD...Waterspouts and wind gusts 34 knots or greater.

SOURCE...Radar.

IMPACT...Waterspouts can easily overturn boats and create locally
hazardous seas. Small craft could be damaged in briefly
higher winds and suddenly higher waves.

* Severe thunderstorms will remain over mainly open waters.
properties.instruction:
Move to safe harbor until hazardous weather passes.

Report severe weather to the Coast Guard or the National Weather
Service. You can also share your report with NWS Miami on Facebook
and Twitter.

properties.areaDesc: Northern Lake Including Gravelly Valley; Eastern Lake Including Clearlake and Middletown
properties.headline: Red Flag Warning issued October 14 at 11:41AM PDT until October 15 at 2:00PM PDT by NWS Eureka CA
properties.description:
The National Weather Service in Eureka has issued a Red Flag
Warning, which is in effect from 4 AM to 2 PM PDT Thursday. a
Fire Weather Watch has also been issued. This Fire Weather Watch
is in effect from late Thursday night through Friday afternoon.

* AFFECTED AREA...Fire weather zones 418 including Lake Pillsbury,
419 including the City of Clearlake, Middletown, Lower Lake,
Indian Valley Reservoir and other areas in eastern Lake County.

* WIND...Sustained winds of 20-25mph with gusts of 30-40mph
possible.

* HUMIDITY...Low overnight recoveries of 30-35% will drop to
15-20% through the morning.

* IMPACTS...any fires that develop will likely spread rapidly.
Outdoor burning is not recommended.
properties.instruction:
A Red Flag Warning means that critical fire weather conditions
are either occurring now, or will shortly. A combination of
strong winds, low relative humidity, and warm temperatures can
contribute to extreme fire behavior.

A Fire Weather Watch means that critical fire weather conditions
are forecast to occur. Listen for later forecasts and possible
Red Flag Warnings.

properties.instruction:

physical stress. If smoke impacts your area; 1) Have a cooling plan

open windows and 2) If you have air conditioning, set on air
recirculation within the home to avoid smoke exposure. Local
officials may have additional guidance.
